LiveFleet timeline

grouped: needs you first, then working, then done

One row per task in the live ledger. Band length is real elapsed time, band colour is state. CNVS stores no state history, only createdAt, completedAt, the current state, and the lane heartbeat file mtime, so each row is the honest two band version: the run interval in its current state colour, split at the heartbeat where a heartbeat exists. A row does not show transitions that were never recorded, and the striped tail means the state is still live right now, not that a transition was observed. Open a row for its note, folder, verify command and heartbeat age.

LiveLane heartbeats, from file mtimes

One row per lane directory under undergrowth-v2/fleet-r*/ plus this workbench. The heartbeat is the newest modification time of that lane's REPORT.md or result.json. A lane whose task is still working and whose heartbeat is older than 10 minutes reads stalled. A lane with no heartbeat file at all, or with no task in the ledger, is shown as exactly that and is never left out: that is how an untracked two-step kimi spawn stops being invisible.

A lane is joined to a task only when its full path appears in exactly one worker prompt file. Where two or more prompts mention the path, the join is ambiguous and this page says so rather than guessing.

LiveOwed and blocked on Luc

Every row carries an owner and a shell check. build.py ran each check during this build and printed the exit code it got, so a row cannot quietly go stale: an item whose check fails is red no matter what its text claims. An item with no automatic check stays amber forever, which is itself the signal that someone wrote a wish instead of a task.

Why every figure says estimate

The cost worker states its own scope as: read-only local CLI session logs; credentials and environment files excluded. Prices come from Fleet-Machine/fleet-r4-ops/cost/PRICES.json, a local table, not from a provider invoice. No task on this canvas carries a cost field, so nothing here can be attributed to one task. The cost worker recorded these limits itself:

  • Some usage sessions have no exact task ID; attribution is session-level until a time-window match is made.
  • A model or cache price was not available for at least one observed session, so usd is null for that entry.
  • Local logs cannot verify provider account, subscription inclusion, discounts, region, invoice currency, or final billed amount.

Collapsed below the fold. Click to open the embedded JSON contract this page is driven by.

Empty on purpose not captured

FieldWhy it is empty
model, every rowThe CNVS ledger has no model field. agentID names a CLI. This is unrecoverable after the fact, not merely missing from this page.
verify exit codeCNVS stores the verify command and, rarely, a cycle count. It never stores the exit code, so a done row is not reproducible from the ledger.
heartbeatNo CLI writes a heartbeat joined to a task id. This page substitutes the mtime of a lane's REPORT.md or result.json, which is a proxy: a worker thinking for 20 minutes without writing looks the same as a dead one.
tokens per taskEvery CLI logs usage somewhere under its home directory, but nothing joins it to a pipe task. The round 4 cost worker reads those logs at session level only.
cost per taskNo per task cost source exists. Session level estimates are all that can be had, and they are labelled estimate everywhere they appear.
current tool call, artifacts, report linkNot present in any source this page reads. The schema section defines them for v1.

UNVERIFIED

  • Model identity for every task, live and historic. The fleet skill says claude means Opus, but no record proves what any node ran.
  • Whether a stalled task is dead, thinking, or waiting on a human. The page can only prove that no file was written, which is not the same thing.
  • That a session counted in the cost window belongs to this project. Attribution is by time overlap at session level, so unrelated work in the same session is included.
  • Every dollar figure. Prices come from a local table, not a provider invoice.
  • Which canvas tasks belong to this project. The tag reads the worker prompt for the project directory or its name, so a task that never writes the path is tagged other canvas work even when it is not.
  • How this page looks at 390 pixels. It was built to the 390 and 1440 rules and checked by reading the CSS, but a CNVS browser node cannot render a 390 pixel viewport, so no agent confirmed it visually. That check is in the owed list, owned by Luc.

undergrowth-v2 workbench. This file is generated output. To change it, edit build.py or template.html in the workbench folder and run python3 build.py --once --project undergrowth-v2, or leave the same command with --loop 15 running. Editing workbench.html by hand is exactly the failure this generator exists to remove: the last hand-maintained workbench on this machine still said "round 3 in progress" in its header while its body documented round 12.

Read-only build: build.py writes one file, workbench.html, and touches nothing else. check.py only reads that file and never rebuilds it.

Self contained: no font, script, stylesheet or image is fetched from anywhere. The page is fully readable with JavaScript switched off; the script below only animates, filters, copies and selects. Every section that is collapsed is a details element, so nothing is hidden behind JavaScript. Opened in a CNVS browser node.
